title: High quality DNA extraction from Sycon capricorn for MinION long read sequencing
author: Erin Vaughn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.i3mcgk6
materials: If performing hybrid assembly, remove 30 mg of tissue from the apical end containing the osculum and transfer to a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube. Extract this sample for Illumina sequencing using the Qiagen AllPrep RNA/DNA/protein kit following the kit’s protocol and eluting in nuclease-free water.

steps.title: Dissect tissue and fix overnight
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, dissect a thin lengthwise axial slice of the specimen and transfer it to a screw‑top vial containing your chosen fixation solution. Incubate the vial overnight at 4 °C with shaking. The next day the sample can be examined under a microscope to check for embryos.

steps.title: Prepare homemade phase‑lock tubes
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL sterilised vacuum grease to a 15 mL Falcon tube and centrifuge at 1500 × g for 2 min to pellet the grease. Set the tube aside for later use as a phase‑lock tube.

steps.title: Add Buffer RLT to tissue
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 mL Buffer RLT per 1 g of tissue to a fresh 15 mL Falcon tube. If the tissue amount is less than 1 g, still add 2.5 mL so that the TissueRuptor probe will be fully immersed.

steps.title: Homogenise tissue and transfer
steps.instruction: Disrupt the tissue with a sterilised disposable TissueRuptor probe set to 4 for 20–30 seconds (or until homogeneous). Immediately pour the homogenate into the pre‑spun phase‑lock tube containing the vacuum grease.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of equilibrated phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol to the homogenised sample. Mix thoroughly by inversion; do NOT vortex.

steps.title: Separate phases by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at 1500 × g for 5 min at room temperature. The vacuum grease should form a barrier between the organic and aqueous phases.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Carefully decant (or pipet with a wide‑bore tip) the upper aqueous phase, which contains nucleic acids, into a 30 mL Corex tube.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with NaOAc
steps.instruction: Add 0.1 volume of 3 M sodium acetate (NaOAc) to the aqueous phase, wrap the tube with parafilm, and mix well by inversion. Do NOT vortex.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 2 volumes of ice‑cold 100 % ethanol, wrap with parafilm, and mix well by inversion. Do NOT vortex.

steps.title: Incubate DNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant, then wash the pellet once with ice‑cold 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Dry and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet until just dry, then resuspend in 500 µL nuclease‑free water. If necessary, heat gently at 50 °C to aid dissolution.

steps.title: Pellet debris removal
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 7700 g for 30 min in a chilled rotor.

steps.title: Transfer DNA solution
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube by pouring or using a wide‑bore pipette tip.

steps.title: Quantify and assess DNA
steps.instruction: Measure genomic DNA concentration with a Qubit fluorometer, then visualise 200 ng of DNA by pulsed‑field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) to confirm high molecular‑weight DNA.
